title: An Int64 of nanoseconds casts to the time of day it counts
description: `cast(pl.Time)` of an Int64 is the time of day with that many nanoseconds (0, 1000 and 86399999999000 give 00:00:00, 00:00:00.000001 and 23:59:59.999999, and `to_physical` gives the count back); NULL in, NULL out. `polars_engine` feeds it `ts % 86400000000 * 1000`, always in range.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; the probe strings; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python) on macOS arm64.
`--diff`: the streaming engine gives what the in-memory one gives, one row at a time and on a column of several morsels.
